title: Identity resolution when the singular ideal escapes
statement: For a Noetherian commutative base R, a finitely presented R-algebra A, a map α:A→Λ and a prime q, if popescuIdeal(α) is not contained in q, then α at q is Popescu resolvable [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

source.place: Definition 07C5 and Situation 07F7; invariance under algebra equivalence

proof.text: Use the intermediate algebra ULift A in the required universe. The canonical equivalence e:ULift A≃A transports finite presentation. The maps e inverse and α∘e compose to α. Invariance of the extended singular ideal gives equality of the two extended singular ideals, hence domination and the assumed escape from q. This is the identity factorization up to the canonical universe equivalence.
